## 2026-07-06 — perf(web): progressive grid rendering + debounced live-sync refetch (Tier 4, final, of the slow-connection fix)
- **Files:** web_ui/src/hooks/useProgressiveList.ts (NEW), web_ui/src/pages/CharactersPage.tsx (render the visible slice + a bottom sentinel), web_ui/src/hooks/useLibrary.ts (debounce the `library_changed` refetch), web_ui/src/styles.css (`.lib-load-more` sentinel row), assets/web_app/** (rebuilt).
- **Reason (Tier 4 of the Starlink/Tailscale plan):** two remaining tail issues after Tiers 1–3 made the *bytes* small. (1) The library grid mapped the **entire** `lib.chars` at once — with a large library that mounts thousands of card + `<img>` nodes, which is heavy to lay out and scroll on a phone even though `loading="lazy"` defers the off-screen image *downloads*. (2) The `library_changed` WebSocket event (fired whenever the desktop app changes anything) called `reload()` immediately, and each reload refetches all three library endpoints — so a burst (a bulk import, a folder reshuffle) hammered the slow uplink with a full reload per event.
- **How fixed:**
  - **Progressive reveal:** new `useProgressiveList(items, batch=60)` hook renders only the first `batch` characters and grows by a batch each time a bottom sentinel nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver` with an 800px `rootMargin` — no scroll handler, no new dependency). It resets to the first chunk whenever the list is replaced (a new search/folder/sort or a live refetch — detected by the `lib.chars` array identity changing). Re-observing on each `count` change lets a tall viewport fill itself instead of stalling on an already-visible sentinel. Only the unbounded characters grid is windowed; folders and groups are bounded so they render whole. `CharactersPage` maps `visibleChars` and renders `{hasMore && <sentinel spinner>}` after the grid.
  - **Debounced live-sync:** the `library_changed` handler now sets a 400 ms trailing timer (cleared/reset on each event, and on unmount) instead of calling `reload()` directly, so a burst of changes coalesces into a single 3-endpoint refetch. Still near-instant for a single change; no more refetch storm over the uplink. (Consistent with the live-sync design — the WS broadcast still drives freshness, just coalesced.)
- **Verification:** web `npm run build` clean (tsc + vite; new hook adds one module); web vitest 27/27. No unit test added for the hook/debounce: the web test suite is deliberately pure-logic-only (jsdom, no `@testing-library/react`, no `IntersectionObserver`), so a hook/observer test would require a new test-only dependency against that convention — verified instead via the type-checker, the production build, and manual scroll testing. No Dart changed in Tier 4.
- **Parity:** web-UI-only — the Flutter desktop library already virtualizes via `GridView`/`ListView.builder`, so there is no desktop counterpart to add.
- **Commit:** (pending user review — staged with Tier 3 in the working tree)

## 2026-07-06 — perf(web): gzip JSON responses + trim the character-list payload (Tier 3 of the slow-connection fix)
- **Files:** lib/services/web/middleware/gzip_middleware.dart (NEW — `GzipMiddleware`), lib/services/web/server_bootstrap.dart (add it as the innermost pipeline middleware), lib/services/web/facade/character_facade.dart (drop `description`/`scenario`/`personality` from the `/api/characters` list map), web_ui/src/hooks/useLibrary.ts (remove the now-dead `LibChar.description` field), test/services/web/gzip_middleware_test.dart (NEW), docs/Rawhide.md unchanged (covered by the Tier-1 bullet).
- **Reason (Tier 3 of the Starlink/Tailscale plan):** two remaining sources of avoidable upload on the home-screen load. (1) The JSON API shipped **uncompressed**: `autoCompress=true` on the dart:io HttpServer only gzips *chunked* responses, but shelf gives every String/byte body a `Content-Length`, so the character-list JSON (and every other JSON endpoint) went out raw — and JSON gzips ~5–10×. (2) The `/api/characters` list — which loads *every* character at once — sent each character's full `description`, `personality`, and `scenario` free-text, none of which the grid renders (`description` was declared on the client `LibChar` type but read nowhere; `scenario`/`personality` weren't even in the type — transmitted then discarded). The editor gets those fields from `/detail`, so the list never needed them.
- **How fixed:**
  - **`GzipMiddleware`** (mirrors the existing `CorsMiddleware`/`SecurityHeaders` style) added as the **innermost** pipeline middleware, so it compresses the handler's response before the outer header middlewares annotate it. It compresses only when it's safe and worthwhile: client sent `Accept-Encoding: gzip`; body is buffered (`Content-Length` present) and ≥ 1 KB; `Content-Type` is text-like (`application/json`, `text/*`, JS, SVG, manifest); and it isn't already `Content-Encoding`'d. It sets `Content-Encoding: gzip`, the new `Content-Length`, and merges `Accept-Encoding` into `Vary`. **WebSocket upgrades** (guarded on the `Upgrade` request header) and any streamed/binary response (no `Content-Length`, or a non-text type such as the avatar PNG/JPEG thumbnails) pass through untouched — so live token streaming and the Tier-1 image thumbnails are unaffected. No double-compression: because the response carries a `Content-Length` (not chunked) with `Content-Encoding` set, dart:io's `autoCompress` skips it. This helps **every** JSON/text endpoint, not just the list.
  - **List trim:** removed `description`/`personality`/`scenario` from the `/api/characters` list map (kept everything the grid uses — id/name/tags/hasAvatar/avatarVersion/folderId/messageCount) and deleted the dead `LibChar.description` client field. A typical character's list entry drops from ~1–5 KB to ~150–250 bytes; combined with gzip on what remains, an ~80-character list goes from potentially hundreds of KB (uncompressed) to a few KB on the wire.
- **Back-compat:** the web UI ships *inside* the same app binary as its server (assets/web_app is bundled), so client and local web-server are always the same version — no mixed-fleet concern here (that rule governs the separate Stoop backend). No app read the removed list fields anyway. gzip is negotiated via `Accept-Encoding`; a client that doesn't send it gets the plain body.
- **No web-asset change:** removing a TypeScript field compiles to identical JS (types are erased), so `assets/web_app` is byte-identical to the Tier-1/2 build — nothing to rebuild/commit there. All of Tier 3 is server-side Dart + one erased type.
- **Verification:** full `flutter analyze` clean; new `GzipMiddleware` unit test 6/6 (compresses large JSON + lossless gzip round-trip; skips no-accept, sub-1KB, non-text, WebSocket-upgrade, and already-encoded); web `npm run build` (tsc) clean with `LibChar.description` gone; web vitest 27/27; Tier-1/2 tests still green.
- **Commit:** (pending user review — staged in the working tree, not yet committed)

## 2026-07-06 — perf(web): persistent service-worker avatar cache + content-versioned URLs (Tier 2 of the slow-connection fix)
- **Files:** web_ui/vite.config.ts (workbox `runtimeCaching` CacheFirst rule + `navigateFallbackDenylist`), web_ui/src/api/client.ts (`avatarUrl` helper), web_ui/src/hooks/useLibrary.ts (`LibChar.avatarVersion`, `LibGroupMember.avatarVersion`), web_ui/src/components/library/LibraryCards.tsx, web_ui/src/components/CharacterPicker.tsx, web_ui/src/pages/CreateGroupChatPage.tsx (thread the version into the avatar `<img>` src), lib/services/web/facade/character_facade.dart (`_avatarVersion` → `avatarVersion` in list JSON), lib/services/web/facade/group_facade.dart (`_memberAvatarVersion` → per-member `avatarVersion`), lib/services/web/util/image_thumbnails.dart (`immutable` cache-control when the request is versioned), assets/web_app/** (rebuilt via `npm run build`).
- **Reason (Tier 2 of the Starlink/Tailscale plan):** Tier 1 shrank avatars and added an ETag, but the PWA service worker only precached the app shell (`globPatterns`), never the runtime `/api/**/avatar` responses — so avatars only lived in the browser HTTP cache and, after its TTL, re-downloaded in full. Goal: make avatars persist on-device for weeks (survive reloads, app close/reopen, and work offline) while never showing a stale picture after an avatar is edited.
- **How fixed (two coupled parts):**
  1. **Content-versioned URLs.** The `/api/characters` and `/api/groups` list JSON now include `avatarVersion` = the avatar file's mtime (ms; 0 when none). The client builds avatar thumbnail URLs via a new `api.avatarUrl(path, w, v?)` helper → `…/avatar?w=400&v=<mtime>`. Because a character's *primary* avatar URL is otherwise stable across a picture swap (same character id), the version makes it content-addressed: change the picture → new mtime → new URL → guaranteed-fresh fetch; unchanged → identical URL → permanent cache hit (zero network — the point on a slow uplink). The server marks versioned thumbnail responses `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, immutable` so the browser doesn't even revalidate. (The multi-avatar `/image` URLs are already immutable-by-id — each distinct image has its own avatarId — so they need no version; `AvatarManager` was left on plain `?w=`. `WorldCard`'s linked-character thumbnail has no version handy and stays unversioned — bounded staleness only, acceptable for that rare surface.)
  2. **Service-worker runtime cache.** Added a Workbox `runtimeCaching` rule (`vite.config.ts`): `urlPattern: /\/api\/.*\/(avatar|image)\?.*w=\d+/`, `CacheFirst`, cache `fpa-avatar-thumbs`, `expiration` {maxEntries 600, maxAge 30d, purgeOnQuotaError}, `cacheableResponse` [0,200]. CacheFirst is correct precisely because the URLs are versioned. The matcher only catches thumbnail (`?w=`) requests, so full-res single portraits (chat header) and the mood-driven `/api/chat/expression-avatar` (no `/avatar` segment, no `w=`) are deliberately excluded — the expression portrait must always reflect the live mood, and it isn't URL-stable per character. Also added `navigateFallbackDenylist: [/^\/api\//]` as a safety belt so an API path can never receive the SPA HTML fallback.
- **Back-compat (per the mixed-fleet rule):** `avatarVersion` is an additive, nullable response field; older apps ignore it. The client treats it as optional — when absent it just omits `&v=` (URL still works, merely uncached-by-version). Older servers ignore the `&v=`/`?w=` query params entirely (shelf routes match on path). No request field became required.
- **Build note:** `assets/web_app` is committed build output that both nightly.yml and build-macos.sh regenerate via `npm run build`; ran it so the tracked assets (and the generated `sw.js`/`workbox-*.js`) reflect the Tier 1 **and** Tier 2 source, and so local `flutter run` serves the new UI. Verified the generated `sw.js` contains the `fpa-avatar-thumbs` CacheFirst rule.
- **Parity note:** web/server-only (service workers + browser caching don't exist on desktop; desktop reads avatars from local disk). No desktop counterpart.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` (full) clean; web `npm run build` succeeds (tsc clean, PWA generateSW emits sw.js + workbox with the avatar rule); web vitest 27/27; Tier 1 thumbnail unit test still 5/5.
- **Commit:** (pending user review)

## 2026-07-06 — perf(web): serve downscaled avatar thumbnails to the web/mobile UI (Tier 1 of the slow-connection fix)
- **Files:** lib/services/web/util/image_thumbnails.dart (NEW — `ThumbnailCache`), lib/services/web/routes/character_routes.dart (`_avatar` + `_avatarImage` → `_thumbs.serve`), lib/services/web/routes/group_routes.dart (`_avatar` → `_thumbs.serve`), lib/services/web/server_bootstrap.dart (construct + inject the cache), lib/services/storage/directories.dart + lib/services/storage_service.dart (new `webThumbnailCacheDir` getter), web_ui/src/components/library/LibraryCards.tsx (grid char `?w=400`, group member `?w=256`), web_ui/src/components/CharacterPicker.tsx, web_ui/src/pages/CreateGroupChatPage.tsx, web_ui/src/components/WorldCard.tsx, web_ui/src/components/AvatarManager.tsx (all grid avatars `?w=256`), test/services/web/image_thumbnails_test.dart (NEW), docs/Rawhide.md.
- **Reason (reported):** Loading the web/mobile home screen over Tailscale on a slow Starlink *upload* took a very long time. Two explore agents traced the cause: the library grid renders one `<img>` per character pointing at `/api/characters/<id>/avatar`, and that endpoint served the **raw full-resolution character-card PNG** — up to ~2048px, hundreds of KB to >1 MB each, *with the entire V2 card base64-embedded in the PNG's `chara` tEXt chunk* (v2_card_service writes it there). So filling a 150px grid tile uploaded ~0.5–1 MB of mostly-wasted pixels + hidden card text; an ~80-character library is ~40–50 MB of host upload just to paint the home screen. The host's uplink is the bottleneck (every byte is uploaded from the desktop through Tailscale to the remote browser).
- **How fixed (Tier 1 — thumbnails):** New `ThumbnailCache` sits in front of the existing avatar `File` resolution. When the client appends `?w=<px>`, it decodes the source once, `copyResize`s to the requested width (never upscales), and re-encodes — **JPEG q82** for opaque art (the common case) or **resized PNG** when a real transparent pixel is present (scanned on the small resized image, not just the alpha-channel flag, so opaque RGBA cards still get tiny JPEGs). Re-encoding also drops the heavy embedded `chara` chunk. Result is generated once and cached to disk (`<root>/cache/web_thumbs`, key = FNV-1a-64 hex of the full source path + width, atomic temp+rename write, stale-if-cache-older-than-source), so subsequent requests are a straight file read. package:image 4.7.2 can't *encode* WebP, hence JPEG/PNG. Every response (thumbnail AND full-res) now also carries an mtime ETag and honors `If-None-Match` → `304`, and thumbnails get `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800` (1 week; safe because the ETag encodes the source mtime). The three avatar handlers (char primary, char multi-avatar image, group member) were unified onto the single `_thumbs.serve(request, file)` call — no parallel per-endpoint image code. Web UI: added `?w=400` to the home-screen character grid and `?w=256` to every other avatar grid (group tiles, character picker, group builder, world cards, avatar manager). Left the large single-portrait displays (chat header / insight portrait) and the mood-driven `_expressionAvatar` full-res on purpose — they're not grids and have bespoke caching. Net: a ~1 MB card PNG → typically ~5–20 KB per tile; the home screen drops from tens of MB to well under 1 MB, and repeat visits revalidate with cheap 304s.
- **Parity note:** web/server-only performance change — the Flutter desktop app reads avatars from local disk (no network), so there is no desktop counterpart to mirror. No visual change on either surface.
- **Not yet done (offered, not built this turn):** Tier 2 (service-worker runtime caching of `/api/**/avatar` so avatars persist across reloads for days), Tier 3 (gzip the currently-uncompressed list JSON + drop the unused description/scenario/personality fields the grid never renders), Tier 4 (grid virtualization/pagination + throttle the `library_changed` full refetch).
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` (full project) clean; `dart fix --dry-run` nothing to fix; web_ui `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; new unit test 5/5 (resize width, JPEG vs PNG selection, no-upscale, disk-cache reuse, stale regeneration).
- **Commit:** (pending user review)

## 2026-07-05 — fix(realism): needs deltas from the last accepted message were reverted when regenerating (or swiping) the next message
- **Files:** lib/services/chat/chat_service_generation.dart (post-gen: re-stamp realism_state.needs.vector with the final post-impact vector), lib/services/chat/chat_service_reprocess.dart (regen: don't let the previous-message baseline clobber the accurate pre-turn needs restore), docs/Rawhide.md.
- **Reason (bug, reported w/ screenshot):** After a message applied a big needs reward (e.g. a bath's Hygiene +55), regenerating the FOLLOWING character message snapped Hygiene back to its pre-bath value (0). Root cause is a stale snapshot: each message's `realism_state` snapshot is captured during the pre-generation realism eval, which runs BEFORE `_runPostGenNeedsChecks` applies that turn's needs impact. So every field in `realism_state` is the final post-turn value EXCEPT `needs.vector`, which is frozen pre-impact. On regen (1:1 path, `_activeGroup == null`), `regenerateLastMessage` restores the *previous accepted message's* `realism_state` as the baseline — and that restore overwrote the live needs vector with the previous turn's PRE-impact needs, discarding the accepted deltas. It clobbered even the correct value that the dedicated `needs_pre_turn_vector` revert (step 1) had just restored. The same stale snapshot is also read by swipe navigation + objective checks via `_restoreRealismStateFromMessage`, so swiping between message versions had the same latent "needs drop".
- **How fixed (two complementary parts):**
  1. **Source (generation):** right after `_runPostGenNeedsChecks(finalResponse)` — the only post-gen needs mutation now that `applyLongGenerationNeedsDecay` is gone — re-stamp `_messages.last.activeMetadata['realism_state']['needs']['vector']` with the now-final `_needsSimulation.vector`. `metadata`/`swipeMetadata[i]` share one map instance (ChatMessage ctor `swipeMetadata ?? [metadata]`), so the in-place update sticks and serializes. Makes the snapshot internally consistent (all fields = final post-turn state) for 1:1 and group, fixing the swipe-navigation and objective-restore consumers, and making the regen fallback correct for new messages. Does NOT affect the needs chip, which uses `needs_pre_turn_vector` as its primary baseline.
  2. **Regen robustness:** track `restoredNeedsFromPreTurn` — set when step 1 restores the rejected message's own `needs_pre_turn_vector` (the accurate pre-turn baseline, always stamped: 1:1 in `sendMessage:3481` pre-tick, group in the realism dance pre-decay). Guard the previous-message `realism_state.needs` restore with `!restoredNeedsFromPreTurn` so it can no longer clobber that value; it stays a fallback only for messages that carry no `needs_pre_turn_vector`. This fixes the reported bug for ALREADY-SAVED chats too (the rejected message's `needs_pre_turn_vector` predates this fix), not just newly generated ones.
- **Parity:** the regen revert block is 1:1-only (`_activeGroup == null`); group regen restores per-speaker needs from `_groupRealism` (already the final post-impact vector), so group never lost the delta. The fix aligns 1:1 regen with group behavior (both now preserve prior accepted needs). Part 1 applies to both modes. WebUI inherits it (regen/swipe route through the same server-side ChatService; needs engine is server-side, no parallel client logic).
- **Hygiene:** 0 new methods (one local bool `restoredNeedsFromPreTurn` + one inline re-stamp block); no dead code; `flutter analyze` clean across all of lib/; needs/realism/parity suites green. Caveat noted to user: an already-corrupted live vector from a regen done *before* this fix can't be retroactively repaired, but it will no longer recur.
- **Commit:** fff74a6

- **Files:** lib/services/chat/realism_evals.dart (narrative `_applyNarrativeResults` + one-shot proposal block: `isPrimary: getPrimaryObjective() == null` — claim the main-quest slot when free, never displace an existing primary; both no-primary prompt variants reframed to ask for an OVERARCHING multi-scene goal, e.g. "get $userName to admit their greatest fear"), lib/services/chat/chat_service_objectives.dart (auto task-gen `taskCount: isPrimary ? 5 : 3`; NEW public `promoteObjective(Objective)` — flips isPrimary in place, demotes any current primary, keeps id + task progress), lib/ui/chat_components/sidebar/story_tools/objective_task_row.dart (`SecondaryObjectiveRow` reworked: takes ChatService+Objective, expandable task list reusing `EditableTaskRow`, n/m progress badge, promote/clear now call promoteObjective/clearObjective directly), objective_panel.dart (new row wiring), lib/ui/dialogs/group_objectives_dialog.dart ("Make primary" → promoteObjective), lib/services/web/facade/chat_tools_facade.dart (promoteObjective(id) via `_withObjective`), lib/services/web/routes/chat_tools_routes.dart ('promote' action), web_ui/src/components/ChatTools.tsx (side quests rendered for the first time: text + n/m + task toggles/remove + Make primary/Clear; summary "(none)" accounts for side quests), web_ui/src/styles.css (.side-quest/.side-quest-label), test/services/chat/realism_evals_test.dart (3 new tests: narrative claims free slot w/ auto tasks, stays secondary when primary exists, one-shot parity), docs/Rawhide.md.
- **Reason (user report):** "An AI objective is not created as a main quest, just a side quest (no subtasks to drive toward completion)." Root cause was three-part: (1) both eval paths hardcoded `isPrimary: false`, so an autonomous goal could never be the driving quest; (2) subtasks actually WERE generated (taskCount 3) and injected/checked, but the desktop side-quest row rendered only bare text — the tasks were invisible, so the feature looked dead; (3) the WebUI didn't render secondary objectives at all. ## 2026-07-05 — fix(realism): fixation (+ spatial stance) bled across chats with the same character on "New Chat"
- **Files:** lib/services/chat/chat_service_session_manage.dart (startNewChat — 1:1 ext-seed branch + group else branch), lib/services/chat_service.dart (add `group_realism_blobs` import for `parseGroupRealismSeeds`), test/services/chat/relationship_service_test.dart (2 new regression tests), docs/Rawhide.md.
- **Reason (bug):** The Realism Engine's fixation (`activeFixation`/`fixationLifespan`) is per-session state stored on `sessions.active_fixation`, and it's injected into the prompt as the `[Background Thought: … has a thought that stays with them about "<fixation>"]` line (behavioral_injection.dart) + the `Current Fixation:` metric (realism_state_injection.dart). It was leaking across chats with the SAME character. The clean home-grid "New Chat" path is safe because it runs `setActiveCharacter`/`setActiveGroup` first (both call `_relationshipService.resetForFreshChat()` / reset `_groupRealism`) BEFORE `startNewChat`. But the **in-chat "New Chat" button** (`chat_page.dart` `_showClearChatConfirmation` → `startNewChat()` with the character/group already active) calls `startNewChat` directly with no preceding reset — and `startNewChat` itself never cleared fixation:
  - **1:1:** the ext-seed branch re-seeds bond/trust via `seedFromCardV2OrExt`, which by design only touches affection/long-term/trust + tiers. It leaves `_activeFixation`, `_fixationLifespan`, `_spatialStance`, `_pendingTrustRepair`, and the long-term/decay counters untouched. Those carried over from the previous conversation and were then persisted onto the new session by the `_saveChat()` at the end of `startNewChat`.
  - **Group:** `startNewChat` never reset the `_groupRealism` map, so every member's per-char fixation (and the rest of their evolved bond/trust/emotion/needs) carried over from the prior session and was re-serialized into the new session's `group_realism_state`.
- **How fixed:** (1) 1:1 branch — call `_relationshipService.resetForFreshChat()` immediately BEFORE `seedFromCardV2OrExt(...)`: reset zeroes every register (incl. fixation/spatial/pending/counters), the seed then restores bond/trust from the card. Mirrors `setActiveCharacter`'s reset-before-load ordering. (2) Group branch — reset `_groupRealism = parseGroupRealismSeeds(_activeGroup!.defaultMemberRealismState)` so each member starts from the group's default baselines (which carry affection/trust/needs but never a fixation). Deliberately NOT routed through `_loadGroupRealismStateFromSession(null)` because `defaultMemberRealismState` is perChar-only, so that path would also wipe the live per-char system prompts / RAG priorities / author notes / decay-rate maps; `parseGroupRealismSeeds` pulls just the perChar baselines and leaves group config intact.
- **Parity:** 1:1 and group both now reset per-character realism to baselines on New Chat (bond/trust already did; fixation now does too). WebUI shares the fix automatically — `chat_facade.dart:507` calls the same `ChatService.startNewChat()` (Realism Engine is server-side; no parallel client logic).
- **Why it slipped through:** `test/services/realism_state_test.dart` asserts "runtime arousal/fixation always reset on new chat (even for cards with extensions)" — but against a hand-written `_RealismStateStub.seedForNewChat()` that resets `_activeFixation=''`, NOT the real `ChatService.startNewChat`. The stub encoded the intended behavior; the real wiring diverged. New tests in `relationship_service_test.dart` lock the real sequence: seed-alone leaves fixation set (documents root cause), reset+seed clears fixation/spatial/pending while restoring bond/trust; and a group per-speaker load from fixation-free baselines yields no obsession.
- **Hygiene:** 0 new private methods (reused existing `resetForFreshChat` + `parseGroupRealismSeeds`); no dead code; `flutter analyze` clean on all touched files; `dart fix --dry-run` nothing; relationship (17), session, group-realism, parity, realism-engine, realism-state suites all green (78 in the combined run). Pure Dart logic — no platform-specific surface.
- **Commit:** fe91e4f (Rawhide)

## 2026-07-05 — Home-screen library sort: fix Recent/Import-Date/Messages + persistence (desktop + web)
- **Files:** lib/utils/character_sort.dart (new — pure, tested sort helper: CharacterSortMode enum + sortCharacters with stable name tiebreaks + dateAdded), lib/utils/utils.dart (barrel export), lib/models/character_card.dart (+createdAt runtime field), lib/services/character_repository.dart (hydrate card.createdAt from the row), lib/database/database.dart (getLastActivityPerCharacter: MAX(created_at) -> MAX(updated_at)), lib/ui/widgets/character_card_grid.dart (use the helper; delete inline switch + dead _extractImportEpoch), lib/services/web/facade/character_facade.dart (recent now sorts by real activity instead of list.reversed; importDate uses row.createdAt; delete dead _importEpoch; stable tiebreaks), test/utils/character_sort_test.dart (new, 8), test/services/sort_mode_persistence_test.dart (new, 2), docs/Rawhide.md.
- **Reason:** User reported the home-screen sort options (time added / message count / last interaction) "don't work right and don't persist." Root causes, all confirmed by reading the code: (1) IMPORT DATE parsed a trailing `_<epoch>` out of the image *filename* (_extractImportEpoch), so every card lacking that legacy `<name>_<epochMs>.png` naming — JSON imports, Chub downloads, renamed files — collapsed to epoch 0 and never ordered. The characters table already has a real `createdAt` column. (2) RECENT ACTIVITY read `MAX(sessions.created_at)` — the time each chat was *started* — not `updated_at`, which `_doSaveChat` already bumps to now every turn; so a character chatted-with today inside an older session sank. One-word query fix (data was already there). (3) PERSISTENCE: the stored value was actually fine (UiSettings.setSortMode writes prefs, load() reads it before `initialized` completes, HomePage.initState restores after) — the *visible* non-persistence was modes (1) and (2) never producing a correct order on reopen, so it read as "forgot my sort." (4) The web/mobile CharacterFacade.list had the SAME importDate filename bug AND a worse `recent` that was just `characters.reversed` (insertion order, no activity at all) — fixed to parity using the shared DB helper + row.createdAt.
- **How:** Added a runtime `CharacterCard.createdAt` hydrated by the repo (mirrors dbId; not serialized). Extracted all sorting into a pure `sortCharacters()` helper with a stable case-insensitive name tiebreak on every mode (so the zero-message / no-activity piles stop jittering between rebuilds), used by the desktop grid; `dateAdded()` prefers DB createdAt and falls back to the legacy filename epoch for pre-hydration cards. Fixed the activity query column. Brought the web facade to the same behavior inline (it works on raw Drift rows, which expose createdAt directly). Deleted both now-dead filename-epoch helpers.
- **Verified:** flutter analyze clean on all changed files (only the 3 pre-existing deprecation infos in untouched files remain); dart fix --dry-run nothing; new tests 10/10 (8 sort-order incl. legacy-fallback + tiebreak edge cases; 2 StorageService round-trip proving sortMode survives a simulated relaunch); repo/storage/facade/utils suites 281 green; dead-code grep for _extractImportEpoch/_importEpoch = 0 in code (comments updated). Parity: desktop grid and web facade now sort identically. LIMITATION: verified by unit tests + analyze, not a live GUI drag — the sort logic is now pure and fully covered, and the DB column change is a one-word swap against an already-populated field.

- **Reason:** Design doc §4.4/§8 phase 2 (docs/design/journal-memory.md). Memories now behave like memories: strong feelings resist fading (a "strong" card cools ~7× slower than a mild one), unpinned cards cool one step per maintenance pass, cold cards leave the always-injected hot set but stay semantically searchable and come back re-warmed when the conversation drifts near them, a character in a sad mood preferentially recalls sadness-family memories (nuanced labels mapped through the existing EmotionLabels table), big story beats (bond/trust swings ≥ 12, trust repair, Chance Time, objective completion) trigger an immediate journal pass instead of waiting for the interval, and a fresh journal on an existing long chat reads only the trailing 50 messages instead of the whole history. Everything deterministic — no new LLM judgment anywhere; embeddings remain strictly optional (no-RAG floor intact: hot/pinned injection never needs the sidecar).

## 2026-07-02 — macOS: app never showed its window on Finder/dock launches (disable experimental merged platform/UI thread)
- Files: macos/Runner/Info.plist (`FLTEnableMergedPlatformUIThread` = false).
- Reason: Launched from Finder/dock/Spotlight, the app bounced once and never presented a window — the process ran fine (engine up, DB + characters loaded, ~290 MB, clean stderr, no crash report), but no window appeared. The SAME build launched via `open`/`flutter run` rendered every time, which made it look intermittent/env-dependent.
- Root cause: Flutter 3.41.x defaults the experimental "merged platform/UI thread" mode ON (FlutterEngine.mm: `mergedPlatformUIThread = YES` unless Info.plist `FLTEnableMergedPlatformUIThread` overrides it). In that mode the window fails to present specifically on a LaunchServices double-click (Finder foreground-activation timing); a programmatic `open` dodges it. Likely tipped over by a macOS update applied on the user's reboot.
- Ruled out first (with evidence): the DownloadManager relative-path fix (df1094c) was already in the build (no `models` exception); environment/PATH (a truly bare `env -i` launch still rendered via open); code signing (spctl accepted, codesign OK); off-screen window (single internal Retina display, on-screen saved bounds); a crash (no crash report, clean stderr).
- Fix: opt out in Info.plist → revert to Flutter's stable separate-thread model, which renders in every launch path. Safe regardless — shipping a production desktop app on an experimental rendering mode isn't worth the risk.
- Verified: `flutter build macos --release` ✓; staged the build and the user double-clicked it from Finder → window appears (root cause + fix confirmed end-to-end).
- Commit: (below)

## 2026-07-02 — Web login management: change username/password in the web UI + desktop recovery
- **Files (Dart):** lib/services/web/auth/auth_service.dart (accountInfo, changeCredentials, signOutAllDevices, resetAccount, hardened disableTotp, shared _reauthenticate "sudo gate"), lib/services/web/auth/session_store.dart (revokeOthers — revoke all but the current session), lib/services/web/routes/auth_routes.dart (POST /api/auth/change-credentials; /api/auth/state now returns username+totpEnabled to AUTHENTICATED callers only; 2fa/disable now requires currentPassword+totpCode; shared _credentialChangeResponse mapper), lib/services/web/web_server_host.dart (auth getter is now lazy on the db so desktop management works while the server is stopped; start() reuses the instance), lib/ui/settings/widgets/web_login_section.dart (new — desktop card: show account, Sign out all devices, Reset web login w/ confirm), lib/ui/pages/settings_page.dart (mount the card in the Web Server section, replacing the static "create it in the browser" hint), test/services/web/auth_service_test.dart (+7 tests), test/services/web/session_store_test.dart (+1 test).
- **Files (web):** web_ui/src/pages/AccountPage.tsx (Login-credentials card: username/new password + current-password/TOTP re-auth; 2FA disable flow; "forgot password" pointer to the desktop reset), web_ui/src/styles.css (.auth-note), assets/web_app/* (rebuilt bundle), docs/Rawhide.md.
- **Reason:** There was no way to change the web UI's username or password after first-run setup — not in the web UI and not in the desktop app — and no recovery if it was forgotten. Per the security review with the user: (1) signed-in changes are allowed but ALWAYS re-authenticate with the current password (+ a current TOTP/recovery code when 2FA is on) so a stolen device with a live session cookie can't take over the account; failed re-auths feed the same lockout as login so the endpoint can't brute-force the current password; a password change revokes every OTHER session (SessionStore.revokeOthers) so stale/stolen cookies die with the old password. (2) "Forgot password" recovery lives ONLY in the desktop app (Settings → Web Server → Reset web login): whoever sits at the desktop already owns the database, so local access is strictly a stronger credential than the web password — no network-based reset exists by design. (3) Tailscale-as-authentication was evaluated and rejected (source IP is not identity; shared tailnets ≠ owner; serve terminates on loopback so identity would ride spoofable headers; ngrok path has no tailnet identity; removes defense in depth). Also hardened while here: 2FA disable previously required nothing beyond a live session — a hijacked session could silently strip the second factor; it now demands password + current code (the web bundle ships with the app, so no mixed-fleet concern for this local API).
- **Verified:** flutter analyze → 0 issues in changed files (only the 3 pre-existing deprecation infos in untouched files); dart fix --dry-run → nothing; flutter test test/services/web + test/ui → 153 green (18 auth/session tests incl. the 8 new); web npm run build (strict tsc + vite + PWA) clean; npm test → 27/27. Golden suite untouched (no golden covers the settings page body; CI confirms). Dead-code audit: the old parameterless disableTotp signature replaced (single caller updated); the static Login hint text deleted from settings_page.dart; no orphaned symbols.
- **Commit:** (below)

Responses pass through verbatim (status + machine-readable error codes) so the web UI maps the same codes the desktop does. Avatars for <img> tags use the facade's remembered-token fallback since images can't send headers. Feature scope per user: full parity except analytics; upload is a "coming soon" surface shown only on desktop-width browsers and completely absent on phones.

## 2026-07-01 — Web server can no longer lock you out of the app on launch + fix Finder/dock "models" path crash
- Files: lib/services/web/web_server_host.dart (new `startSafely()` crash-loop-safe start; extracted RemoteSetupResult + LAN-IP helpers so the file did not grow past the 500-line cap — 521→511), lib/services/web/tunnels/remote_setup_result.dart (new — moved value class, re-exported from the host so no consumer import changes), lib/services/web/tunnels/lan_ip.dart (new — `detectPrivateLanIp()` extracted), lib/services/storage/settings/web_server_settings.dart (new persisted `web_server_starting` breadcrumb + getter/setter), lib/main.dart (`_autoStartWebServer` routes through `startSafely(isAutoStart: true)`), lib/ui/pages/settings_page.dart (Enable Web Server toggle routes through startSafely + snackbar/revert on failure), lib/services/download_manager.dart (guard `_ensureTargetDir` against relative/non-absolute paths + never throw; `targetDir` is now a setter that re-ensures).
- Reason: A user on a signed/notarized nightly enabled the Web Server, the app crashed, and then it would not launch at all — the dock icon bounced once and vanished. Investigation (real crash reports + faithful GUI-launch repro via `open --stdout/--stderr`) ruled OUT code signing entirely: the notarized app runs the web server fine in isolation (port binds, ~300 MB healthy). The real trap was a launch-time crash loop: "web server enabled" is persisted the instant the toggle flips, and main.dart auto-starts the server on every launch (post-frame). So if the FIRST start ever fails — a hang in a wedged Tailscale `serve`, a hard native crash mid-bind, anything — the app re-runs that same failing start on every subsequent launch, dying before the window can paint. Since the app never opens, the built-in updater can't rescue it: a permanent, self-inflicted lockout from one bad start. Separately, launching from Finder/dock (working dir `/`) reproduced an unhandled `FileSystemException: Read-only file system` from DownloadManager creating a RELATIVE `models` dir (StorageService.rootPath is still null when the provider constructs it, so `modelsDir.path` is literally `models`); harmless from a terminal (writable cwd) but a real cross-platform bug on every GUI launch.
- How: (1) One shared, crash-loop-safe entry point `WebServerHost.startSafely(port, {isAutoStart})` used by BOTH launch auto-start and the Settings toggle (no parallel path). It sets a PERSISTED "starting" breadcrumb before the risky bind and clears it on success; if a later auto-start launch still sees the breadcrumb set, the previous start never finished (hard crash/kill mid-start), so it disables the server and lets the app open cleanly — the user re-enables from Settings. The start is also time-boxed (25 s) and any error/timeout disables the server and tears down the half-started state. This closes the lockout for hangs (timeout), Dart exceptions (catch), AND hard native crashes (next-launch breadcrumb). The toggle additionally shows a snackbar + reverts when a manual start fails. (2) DownloadManager._ensureTargetDir now no-ops on a non-absolute path (the transient relative `models`) and never throws; `targetDir` became a getter/setter so the provider's re-point to the real absolute StorageService.modelsDir re-ensures the dir — reusing the existing method, no new ones.
- Anti-god-file: web_server_host.dart was already 521 lines; rather than grow it, extracted the standalone RemoteSetupResult value class and the pure LAN-IP detection into their own focused files (RemoteSetupResult re-exported from the host so no consumer import changes). Net host size 521 → 511.
- Verified: flutter analyze clean (full project + per-file); dart fix --dry-run per changed file → Nothing to fix; flutter build macos (debug) → ✓ Built; dead-code audit — startSafely/setWebServerStarting/webServerStarting/detectPrivateLanIp all referenced, no leftover _detectLanIp/_is172Private, no duplicate RemoteSetupResult. The two remaining direct start() callers (the remote-setup tutorial + the port-change restart) were intentionally left as-is; they self-heal via the next-launch breadcrumb. NOTE: the underlying "first start" failure itself was NOT reproducible on a clean machine — it appears specific to the user's dual-run dev setup (flutter run debug + installed nightly sharing one bundle id → one SQLite DB / prefs / port 8085). These fixes make such a failure non-catastrophic rather than chasing the elusive trigger.

## 2026-07-01 — Web/mobile UI: fix hang when a Chaos "Chance Time" event fires
- Files (Dart): lib/services/chat_service.dart (durable web chance-time accessors + double-accept race guard), lib/services/web/facade/chat_facade.dart (state.chanceTime + acceptChanceTime), lib/services/web/routes/chat_routes.dart (POST /api/chat/chance-time/accept), lib/services/web/web_server_host.dart (`chance_time` WS broadcast on park/release edge), lib/ui/widgets/chance_time_overlay.dart (speaker attribution unified onto ChatService.chanceTimeSpeakerName)
- Files (web): web_ui/src/components/ChanceTimeModal.tsx (new reveal-card modal), web_ui/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx (open/reveal/accept + reconnect recovery + failure-reopen), web_ui/src/api/ws.ts (`pending` field), web_ui/src/styles.css (.chance-* styles), assets/web_app/* (rebuilt PWA bundle)
- Reason: A Discord user reported the web app hangs when Chaos is enabled — the prompt sends but no reply ever comes; they correctly guessed it was waiting for the desktop-only "Accept your fate" button. Root cause: when chaos rolls a Chance Time event, ChatService.sendMessage parks on `_chanceTimeCompleter` (chat_service.dart:3133) and refuses to generate until someone accepts fate, and that completion only ever came from the DESKTOP wheel overlay's button. The web/mobile UI drives the SAME shared ChatService over HTTP/WS but was never told a Chance Time was pending, had no wheel/button, and no endpoint to resolve it — so the parked send hung forever (and, because the instance is shared, the wheel actually popped on the unattended desktop; clicking it there would unstick the phone, which is why it felt intermittent/haunted). Fix, keeping the accept path shared and the simulation untouched: (1) ChatService exposes a durable `isAwaitingChanceTime`, a pre-picked `webChanceTimeDisplay` (sampled from the same pool via the side-effect-free spinWheelEvents(); desktop still spins its own wheel — presentation differs, logic is one path), and `acceptPendingChanceTime`; (2) web_server_host's existing ChatService listener broadcasts a `chance_time` WS event on the park/release edge, and /api/chat/state carries `chanceTime` so a reconnecting phone recovers; (3) new bodyless POST /api/chat/chance-time/accept; (4) a React reveal-card modal (tease → reveal → "Accept Your Fate") that pops instantly, survives the phone sleeping through the live event, reopens if the accept POST fails, and auto-closes if another surface accepts first. Also hardened applyChanceTimeResult against a double-accept race (desktop + web resolving the one shared completer would otherwise throw completing an already-completed Completer) and de-duplicated the event's speaker attribution into a single ChatService.chanceTimeSpeakerName getter (was inline in the desktop overlay). 1:1/group parity preserved (attribution follows the upcoming group speaker exactly as the desktop wheel did).
- Verified: `flutter analyze` on all 5 changed Dart files → No issues found; `dart fix --dry-run` per file → Nothing to fix; web `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit + vite) clean; web `npm test` (vitest) → 19/19 pass; dead-code grep (every new symbol referenced; old inline attribution pattern gone). LIMITATION: a live end-to-end trigger needs the desktop backend running with Chaos on + an RNG hit, which can't be forced in a headless check — the flow is verified by code review + the build/test gates, not a live chaos event.

Runtime already read by mid, so this makes the WRITER match the READER — creator seeds finally take effect and 1:1↔group behavior converges. Existing groups are unchanged until edited (their realism was already defaulted by the bug); editing the new tab recovers/migrates them. ## 2026-06-30 — Objectives: subtask generator wrote tasks for the user instead of the character
- **Files:** lib/services/chat/objective_proposal.dart (`generateObjectiveTasks` prompt); docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing note).
- **Reason:** Users reported that generating subtasks for an objective produced steps for the USER/player to perform rather than the character. Investigated whether this was model collapse (reporter ran a 13B) or a prompt bug — it is a prompt bug, and the same shared generator feeds BOTH user-created and autonomous objectives, so neither path was safe. Root cause: every other part of the objectives system names the character as the actor — the autonomous proposal prompt in realism_evals.dart asks for "a goal $charName independently wants to pursue", and the objective injection (author_note_builder.dart) frames goals as "[AUTONOMOUS GOAL (this character genuinely wants this — pursue it actively)]" / "Guide the narrative toward completing the current task". But `generateObjectiveTasks` was the lone outlier: it used "You are a quest designer… designing quest tasks", asked for "tasks that must be completed to achieve the objective", and listed "Character: $charName" only as a context label, NEVER stating that $charName is the one who performs the tasks and never mentioning the user at all. In the overwhelming majority of training data, "quest tasks the player completes" are the PLAYER's to do, so models — a 13B especially, but not exclusively — default to writing the steps for the user. That's faithful prompt-following, not degenerate output, so model collapse is disproved as the cause (a larger model would guess character-agency from context more often, masking the same latent bug). Fix rewrites the prompt to (1) drop the player-biased "quest designer/quest tasks" framing in favor of "designing a character's own next steps", (2) state explicitly that the tasks are concrete in-story actions $charName personally carries out — the CHARACTER, not the user, (3) name $userName as the forbidden subject ("NEVER an instruction/request/task assigned to $userName"), (4) require third-person with $charName as actor, and (5) make the example template actor-explicit ("[a specific action $charName takes]"). One shared prompt → fixes user-created and autonomous identically; no parallel path. Preserves the test-asserted substrings ($charName in the prompt, "uncensored" in the nsfw preamble).
- **Gates:** `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` on objective_proposal.dart (Flutter 3.41.1) — No issues found. `flutter test test/services/chat/objective_proposal_test.dart` — all 15 tests pass (incl. the prompt-content asserts for charName + nsfw "uncensored"). No new methods; reused the existing getUserName callback (already on the leaf) for the user name.

## 2026-06-30 — Realism evals: arousal/Lust crept up on non-sexual turns + never decayed
- **Files:** lib/services/chat/realism_evals.dart (arousal instruction in `evaluateEmotionalStateCall` + `evaluateOneShotCall`); docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing note).
- **Reason:** A user reported Lust rising +5 while talking about food. Root cause is two-fold and both live in the arousal prompt. (1) Unlike the relationship_delta and trust_delta rubrics — which each carry an explicit "⚠ Default to 0 for normal conversation / 0: ONLY a truly neutral exchange" anchor — the `arousal_delta` instruction had NO zero anchor. It only said "Be bold with arousal deltas" and listed exclusively sexual/intimate examples (whispered compliment = +3, kiss = +10…). With no instruction that non-sexual content is 0, models dutifully assigned a small positive (+3/+5) to mundane turns. (2) There is NO passive arousal decay anywhere: `setArousalLevel` is only ever called by the eval's additive `arousalLevel + arousalDelta` (realism_evals.dart) and by climax reset to -3 (`NsfwService.applyClimaxEffects`) — confirmed by grepping every `setArousalLevel`/arousal-mutation site. So once arousal ratcheted up it stayed up forever unless a climax occurred; small per-turn positives accumulated and the Lust meter stuck high. Fix adds two guard lines to the arousal instruction in BOTH the emotional-state eval and the fused one-shot eval (parity): an explicit "⚠ Default to 0 — non-sexual/platonic/mundane content (food, work, errands, small talk) is 0, NOT a small positive," and "⚠ Arousal does NOT linger on its own — if current arousal is above 0 and this turn isn't sexual/charged, return a NEGATIVE delta (e.g. -5 to -10) to cool toward neutral." This mirrors the existing default-to-0 pattern the other two deltas already use, fixes both the "+5 on food" symptom and the underlying "never comes down" gap, and stays fully model-driven (no new state/code, no decay-timer to keep in 1:1↔group sync). The two added lines are byte-identical across the two eval paths, preserving one-shot vs multi-call parity. Arousal eval only runs when `nsfwCooldownEnabled`, so non-NSFW chats are unaffected.
- **Gates:** `flutter analyze` NOT runnable in this remote container (no Dart/Flutter toolchain). Changes are additional string literals appended inside an existing ternary (no structural/syntax change, no new methods/state, no dead code). Edited regions re-read to confirm well-formed literals and identical new guidance in both paths. NOTE (out of scope, flagged not fixed): lib/services/chat/prompt_injection/nsfw_injection.dart:69-71 has pre-existing dead code — `protectiveWindowActive = 0 > 0 || 0 > 0` is always false, making the 72-75 block unreachable.

- **Files:** lib/services/chat/llm_eval_engine.dart (`evaluateNeedsImpactCall` — added a shared `climaxGuidance` string injected into BOTH the main and the critique needs-impact prompts; added a positive `is_climax: true` example to each; extended both JSON schemas with `"refractory_turns"`).

The prompt asked the model for an `is_climax: true/false` field but NEVER defined what a climax is or when to set it. So models — especially reasoning/"thinking" models, which won't guess at an undefined field — returned `is_climax: false` almost every time. Result: `onClimax` never fired, arousal was never reset, the other realism evals kept adding +15…+25 arousal per turn, and the Lust bar stayed pinned at 95-100 forever with no cooldown. Secondary bug: the parser already looked for `refractory_turns`/`crashTurns` but the prompt never asked the model to emit it, so cooldown length silently always defaulted to 5. Fix adds explicit climax criteria (mirroring the "high arousal is NOT climax — climax only on actual sexual release" rule the emotional/physical evals in realism_evals.dart already use), restricts detection to `$charName`'s OWN orgasm (not the partner's/user's), a concrete positive example, and has the model emit `refractory_turns` (3-7). One shared string used by both prompt branches → no duplication. Needs-impact runs identically for 1:1 and per-speaker group, so parity is preserved automatically.
- **Gates:** `flutter analyze` on llm_eval_engine.dart + needs_impact_evaluator.dart — No issues found. No new methods added; no dead code introduced.
- **Commit:** 741e884

## 2026-06-27 — Golden CI: fix 2 failing widget goldens (PR #70) + image-decode determinism
- **Files:** test/golden/support/golden_app.dart (new top-level `_precacheMountedImages(tester)` helper + call in `pumpGolden` after settle, before capture); .github/workflows/update-goldens.yml (new — manual `workflow_dispatch` to regenerate goldens on the exact ubuntu-latest + Flutter 3.41.1 runner and upload only the changed PNGs as an artifact, no auto-push).
- **Reason:** PR #70's `Widget Golden Tests` job failed on exactly 2 test cases / 3 PNGs. (1) `sidebar/realism.{dark,light}.png` — a *legitimate* shift from #29 (the sidebar now shows live Needs SCORES; I removed the old `NeedsDecayRatesSection` decay-slider block from realism_section.dart), so the baseline simply needs re-blessing. (2) `dialogs_more/background_settings.light.png` — NOT my regression: BackgroundSettingsDialog renders a GridView of 20 real `Image.asset` thumbnails, and the harness never precached images. `pumpAndSettle` does not await async image-decode frames, so the capture snapshotted a random decode stage — the smoking gun was the baseline pair itself (light 354 KB with art decoded vs dark 24 KB blank, despite identical theme-independent content). Fixed the flakiness at the source by precaching every mounted Image inside `tester.runAsync` before capture (no-op for image-less goldens → all other baselines stay byte-identical; unresolved providers like Image.network are swallowed). Goldens regenerated on the CI Linux runner (never the Mac — anti-aliasing differs) because the widget goldens are `@TestOn('linux')` and cannot run on macOS at all.
- **Gates:** `flutter analyze` on golden_app.dart — No issues found; update-goldens.yml validated as well-formed YAML. Golden pixels themselves validated by the post-regen CI run (cannot execute on macOS).
- **Commit:** 741e884

- **Backend** (`voice_facade.dart`, new): `status()` (ttsEnabled/ttsEngine/sttEnabled/sttAvailable); `speak(text, voiceKey)` → `TtsService.generateAudioFile` bytes + MIME (wav, or mpeg for ElevenLabs), null when TTS off; `transcribe(bytes, ext)` → writes a temp file and calls STT, cleans up. Guards: empty text / disabled / empty body / STT unavailable all return null.
- **Backend** (`stt_service.dart`): new public `transcribeAudioFile(path)` wrapping the existing private `_transcribe` (so the web can transcribe a client-uploaded file; the host recorder path is unchanged). Single public method, no parallel impl.
- **Routes** (`voice_routes.dart`, new): `GET /api/voice/status`; `POST /api/tts/speak` (JSON in, audio bytes out); `POST /api/stt/transcribe` (raw audio body, `?ext=`, capped at uploadMaxBytes, JSON `{text}` out).
- **Wiring**: `VoiceFacade` added to the facades barrel, `WebServerDeps`, `server_bootstrap` (registered when present), and `WebServerHost` (new `setTtsService`/`setSttService`, built when both are injected); `main.dart` injects both into the host (mirrors the legacy server's existing TTS/STT wiring).
- **Frontend** (`VoiceControls.tsx`, new): `SpeakButton` (synthesize + play via `new Audio(blobUrl)`) and `MicButton` (MediaRecorder → upload → transcript), the latter gated on `window.isSecureContext`. `client.ts` gained `postForBlob` (JSON→binary) and `postBlob` (raw upload→JSON). `ChatPage.tsx` fetches `/api/voice/status`, shows 🔊 on AI replies when TTS is on, and a 🎤 in the input when STT is usable + secure context; `.icon-btn.mic.recording` pulse CSS.
- **Tests**: new `voice_facade_test.dart` (status flags, speak no-op when off, transcribe no-op when unavailable/empty). New `FakeSttService` (avoids the real ctor's platform-channel AudioRecorder, which throws MissingPluginException headless).
- **Verification**: `flutter analyze` (web + main + stt + tests + fakes) clean; `flutter test test/services/web` 61/61; `dart fix --dry-run` nothing to fix; `web_ui` tsc + vite build green.

## 2026-06-25 (fix(ci/macos): make Nightly .pkg NON-RELOCATABLE — the bundle-id split was forking the install into /Applications/*.localized/)
- **Files changed**: .github/workflows/nightly.yml — "Build macOS PKG" step now builds a non-relocatable component pkg via `pkgbuild --root <staged .app> --component-plist <plist with BundleIsRelocatable=false>` instead of `pkgbuild --component <app>` (which is relocatable by default). Stages the signed .app with `ditto` (preserves signature + framework symlinks).
- **Root cause (a regression I introduced)**: the earlier bundle-id split (`com.linux4life1.frontPorchAi` -> `.nightly`) fixed the stable/nightly collision but broke the FIRST transition update. The relocatable pkg looks up the NEW id, doesn't find it (installed app still has the OLD id), then refuses to overwrite the different-id app at /Applications/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app and FORKS the payload into /Applications/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.localized/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app. Observed live on the maintainer's Mac: new build (6788a17, .nightly id) landed in the .localized folder while the old bare app (38f015a, shared id) stayed put and kept being launched.
- **Fix verified LOCALLY (not just reasoned)**: built both pkg variants on this Mac and expanded them. `--component` -> `PackageInfo` has `<relocate><bundle id=".nightly"/></relocate>` (relocation ON, forks). `--root`+component-plist with BundleIsRelocatable=false -> `<relocate/>` empty (relocation OFF, deterministic overwrite at the declared path). The empty `<relocate/>` is Apple's documented signal for a non-relocatable component. (Full behavioral install test needs root; structural proof is definitive at the packaging layer.)
- **Why relocation-OFF is right here**: combined with the per-channel bundle id, it gives both properties we need — no stable/nightly id ambiguity AND a deterministic install path that overwrites the old app in place on the transition. Nightly always lives at /Applications/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app, so forcing that path loses nothing.
- **Maintainer machine cleanup**: the correct 6788a17 build was already installed at /Applications/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.localized/...; moved it to the canonical /Applications/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app and removed the old bare app + the .localized folder (sudo, root-owned pkg files).
- **Scope**: nightly.yml only. release.yml's macOS pkg keeps the same id forever (stable->stable finds the id and overwrites in place), so it doesn't hit the transition fork — but the same non-relocatable hardening could be applied for robustness if desired. Must mirror to main's nightly.yml. Requires a fresh nightly build to produce a non-relocatable pkg; only THAT pkg installs cleanly over an old-id app.
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

Flutter SDK + pip are also re-fetched each run (adds a few minutes). Accepted per maintainer preference (correctness > CI time).
- **Scope**: must be applied to BOTH Rawhide and main copies of release.yml (release runs from the tag, cut from main). beta-release.yml still has its ml-engines cache — left per standing "ignore beta" instruction.

## 2026-06-25 (fix(ci): REMOVE the ML-engines cache entirely from nightly.yml — guarantee no stale-app class of bug, per maintainer preference)
- **Files changed**:
  - .github/workflows/nightly.yml — deleted the `Cache ML Engines` (`actions/cache@v4`, id `ml-cache`) step, and rewrote `Bundle ML Engines` to ALWAYS build sidecars from source: removed the `cache-hit` restore branch, the `CACHE_DIR`/`CACHE_HIT`/`SIDECAR_DIRS` variables, and the cache-save block. The PyInstaller/cargo sidecar build now runs unconditionally every nightly.
  - docs/Rawhide.md — updated the user-facing bullet ("compile and ship the app fresh on every run — the risky caching that caused this is gone entirely").
- **Why (supersedes the earlier sidecars-only fix in this same changelog below)**: the earlier fix (cache only the sidecar dirs, bump key to v2) was correct and safe, but the maintainer chose to remove ML-engines caching outright — accepting the extra ~10-20 min sidecar compile time per nightly to eliminate the entire "everything reports current but the app is stale" failure mode for good. For a once-a-day build that is the right trade. Confirmed root cause stands: the old step did `cp -r build_path/*` in/out of the cache, and build_path contains the compiled Flutter app, so cache hits restored a stale app over the fresh `flutter build` output (proven: published nightly-rawhide.20260625 .pkg's App binary baked appVersion was rawhide.20260621).
- **Why the OTHER caches are kept (safe)**: the Flutter SDK cache, flutter-pub cache, setup-python pip cache, and Swatinem rust-cache (embed_server) only cache build *inputs* (SDK, packages, cargo target keyed by Cargo.lock+source), never the compiled Flutter app — so they cannot produce a stale-app artifact. Removing them would add large time for zero safety gain.
- **Process note / earlier failed verification**: an initial workflow_dispatch (run 28159396808, headSha 546ee13) ran the OLD workflow because the Rawhide commits (62a70f0 bundle-id, 9f3e833 sidecars-only) had been committed LOCALLY but not pushed; that run hit the old `ml-engines-` cache and shipped stale code again. Rawhide has since been pushed (546ee13..9f3e833) and this removal sits on top.
- **Scope**: nightly.yml only. beta-release.yml still has the cache (dormant; left per instruction). release.yml has no ML cache. Must also be mirrored to main's nightly.yml (scheduled cron uses main's definition).
- **Verification**: `yaml.safe_load` ✓; grep confirms ZERO remaining references to `ml-cache`/`ml-engines-cache`/`CACHE_DIR`/`CACHE_HIT`/`SIDECAR_DIRS`. Build body left intact (always-run). End-to-end proof still requires a real CI run with NO cache → download artifact → confirm baked appVersion == release tag. No app/Dart code changed.
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

## 2026-06-25 (fix(ci): ML-engines cache was caching the whole build dir — froze the compiled app, shipping stale nightlies on every platform)
- **Files changed**:
  - .github/workflows/nightly.yml — the "Bundle ML Engines" step now caches/restores ONLY the sidecar dirs (`piper whisper_stt embed_server sentiment_classifier dt_grpc_client`) instead of `cp -r build_path/*`. Restore (cache hit) and save (cache miss) both loop over `$SIDECAR_DIRS`; the freshly-built Flutter app (the `.app` on macOS; `front_porch_ai.exe` + `data/app.so` on Windows) is never copied from/to the cache. Cache key bumped `ml-engines-` → `ml-engines-v2-` (and restore-keys) to drop the poisoned caches in one clean miss.
  - docs/Rawhide.md — user-facing "Nightly builds now actually ship the latest code" bullet.
- **Root cause (THE big one — verified against the published artifact)**: the `actions/cache` ML-engines cache key only hashes the Python/Rust *sidecar* sources, so it stays valid for days/weeks. But the step did `cp -r "$CACHE_DIR/"* "$build_path/"` on hit and `cp -r "$build_path/"* "$CACHE_DIR/"` on miss — and `build_path` ALSO contains the freshly-compiled Flutter app. So on every cache hit the step copied a STALE app (frozen at the last cache-miss day) over the fresh `flutter build` output. The release tag/exe-version-resource are computed from the current run (today), but the actual compiled `app.so`/`App` binary was the old cached one → stale code shipped under a fresh label. Different platforms froze on different days (Windows ≈ rawhide.20260619, macOS ≈ rawhide.20260621). PROOF: extracted the published `nightly-rawhide.20260625.ac2d41f` macOS `.pkg`; its `App` binary's baked `appVersion` was `rawhide.20260621.38f015a` (it did contain newer features like `turnorder`, confirming "recent-but-frozen code", not a sed/version-patch failure).
- **Why this is the primary cause of the update loop**: the in-app updater compares the running app's baked `appVersion` to the latest release tag. Because the baked version was frozen behind the advancing tag, `_isNewerVersion(tag, baked)` was permanently true — "Update Available" could never clear, on EVERY platform, even with a flawless install. (The separately-fixed macOS shared-bundle-id and the Windows shared-AppId issues are real but secondary; they prevented the overwrite, this froze the payload.)
- **Scope**: nightly.yml fixed here. beta-release.yml has the identical pattern (lines ~132-138 restore, ~312-314 save) — left untouched per maintainer instruction ("ignore beta, old cruft"); flagged for parity if beta is revived. release.yml (stable) has NO ML-engines cache (always rebuilds sidecars), so stable was never affected.
- **CRITICAL follow-up — must also land on `main`**: like all nightly packaging changes, scheduled cron runs use main's workflow definition; this fix must be mirrored to main's nightly.yml to take effect on the daily build.
- **Verification**: YAML validated (`yaml.safe_load` ✓). Logic reviewed: `$SIDECAR_DIRS` defined before the if/else so both branches see it; `rm -rf` before each `cp -r` avoids nested-dir duplication on re-copy. CANNOT be fully verified without a real CI run — the proof-of-fix is: trigger a manual nightly (workflow_dispatch), download the artifact, and confirm the baked `appVersion` equals the release tag. No app/Dart code changed.
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

## 2026-06-25 (fix(ci/macos): give Rawhide Nightly its own bundle identifier — ends the macOS Nightly update loop)
- **Files changed**:
  - .github/workflows/nightly.yml — in the "Rename macOS app bundle for Rawhide Nightly" step (before code signing), added one PlistBuddy line that sets `CFBundleIdentifier` to `com.linux4life1.frontPorchAi.nightly` on `FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app`. Stable still ships `com.linux4life1.frontPorchAi`. Previously BOTH stable (`front_porch_ai.app`) and Nightly (`FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app`) carried the identical bundle id, so `/Applications` had two distinct .app bundles claiming one identity.
  - docs/Rawhide.md — added a user-facing "macOS Nightly updates now actually replace the running app" bullet (feeds the in-app Update dialog).
- **Reason / root cause** (verified on the user's Mac): the in-app macOS updater installs by `open <pkg>` → Installer.app. The Nightly `.pkg` is a relocatable component package keyed on `CFBundleIdentifier`. With two on-disk bundles sharing `com.linux4life1.frontPorchAi`, bundle relocation could not unambiguously target the running Nightly bundle, so the `.pkg` payload never reliably overwrote `/Applications/FrontPorchAI-Rawhide.app`. Net effect: the installed Nightly stayed on the old build (confirmed: installed `rawhide.20260621.38f015a` while latest published was `rawhide.20260625.ac2d41f`) and the app re-prompted "Update Available" forever — the macOS twin of the just-fixed Windows shared-AppId loop. A distinct per-channel id makes relocation unambiguous (exactly one bundle claims `.nightly`), so the Installer overwrites the Nightly bundle in place wherever it lives (relocation deliberately left ON — the macOS analogue of the Windows `/DIR` "install where it already lives" fix).
- **Data safety**: app is NOT sandboxed (macos/Runner/Release.entitlements: `com.apple.security.app-sandbox`=false), so chats/characters live in `~/Documents/FrontPorchAI-Beta` keyed by the dir + `isPreRelease`, NOT by bundle id — untouched. Only macOS NSUserDefaults (`~/Library/Preferences/<bundle-id>.plist`) is bundle-id-keyed → a one-time Nightly app-settings reset on changeover (documented). Verified no Dart/Swift code reads the bundle id (grep: only Info.plist + AppInfo.xcconfig reference it).
- **CRITICAL follow-up — must also land on `main`**: scheduled (cron) nightly runs execute the workflow *definition* from the default branch (`main`), checking out Rawhide only for source. This new packaging STEP therefore will NOT run on scheduled builds until the same edit is mirrored to `main`'s nightly.yml (see the header comment in nightly.yml). Until then, only a `workflow_dispatch` run from Rawhide would exercise it.
- **Scope note**: beta-release.yml (ad-hoc signed, app name `FrontPorchAI.app`, shares id+path with stable — latent but unreported) and release.yml (stable, canonical id) were intentionally NOT touched. Per-channel parity for beta/stable is offered as a follow-up rather than changing release pipelines that can't be locally verified.
- **Verification**: YAML/shell reviewed; PlistBuddy `Set :CFBundleIdentifier` runs before the signing step that seals Info.plist. Full effect can only be confirmed by a notarized macOS CI run (cannot be reproduced on the local machine). No Dart code changed → `flutter analyze` surface unaffected.
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

## 2026-06-24 (fix: macOS notarization — normalize PyInstaller frameworks (duplicate root binary caused "ambiguous bundle"))
- **Files changed**:
  - .github/workflows/nightly.yml — macOS "Code Sign macOS App" step, framework handling. Third iteration. The previous "rebuild Versions/A" attempt (run 28084643719) hard-failed at the new local verify gate with the real diagnostic: `codesign ... Python.framework: bundle format is ambiguous (could be app or framework)` plus an `ls -laR` dump. **The dump corrected the whole theory**: these frameworks are NOT flat — they are already versioned (`Versions/3.11/Python` is the real binary, with `Versions/Current`). The actual culprit is that PyInstaller *also* drops a DUPLICATE real `Python` binary (and real `Resources`) at the framework ROOT; a real Mach-O at the bundle root looks app-like while `Versions/` looks framework-like, so codesign can't seal it ("ambiguous") and notarization then reports "signature invalid." My own prior code had also created a junk `Versions/A/Resources/Info.plist` (the Info.plist synth block hardcoded `Versions/A` even though the real version is `3.11`). **New fix**: discover the real version dir dynamically (the dir under `Versions/` holding the real principal binary), point `Versions/Current` at it, convert the root `Python`/`Resources`/`Headers`/`Modules` entries into SYMLINKS into `Versions/Current` (dropping the duplicate root binary — this is what clears the ambiguity), remove any stray `Versions/A`, then seal + `codesign --verify --deep --strict`. Verified the symlink normalization locally against a faithful reproduction of the dumped structure (root entries become symlinks, Current→3.11, junk A removed, root binary resolves to the real one).
- **Reason**: the "ambiguous bundle" error (surfaced by the local verify gate added in the prior commit) revealed the frameworks were versioned-with-a-duplicate-root-binary, not flat; the fix is to normalize to canonical symlink layout, not to rebuild structure.
- **Verification**: `python3 yaml.safe_load` parses; extracted shell `bash -n` clean; normalization logic unit-tested locally (correct canonical layout produced). Autonomous build loop continuing.
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

## 2026-06-24 (fix: macOS notarization — rebuild flat PyInstaller frameworks into sealed Versions/A bundles)
- **Files changed**:
  - .github/workflows/nightly.yml — macOS "Code Sign macOS App" step, framework handling. Follow-up to the copy-out attempt earlier today, which FAILED: run 28083431366 still got status=Invalid, same five `*/Python.framework/Python` "The signature of the binary is invalid." errors, even though codesign reported success on the copied-out standalone binaries ("✓ signed via copy-out" appeared for all 5). Root cause refined: these are **flat** frameworks (principal Mach-O at the framework root, no Versions/A). Apple validates that binary *as the principal of a framework bundle*; a flat framework cannot be sealed by codesign ("bundle format is ambiguous"), so signing the bare Mach-O — in place or copied out — never satisfies the notary. **New fix**: rebuild the canonical `Versions/A` structure (move root contents into Versions/A, create `Versions/Current → A` + top-level `Python`/`Resources`/`Headers` symlinks), synthesize a minimal Info.plist if PyInstaller didn't ship one, sign nested `.so`/`.dylib` first, then `codesign` the framework itself so it is sealed as a real framework (which also signs the principal binary). Added a HARD local `codesign --verify --deep --strict` gate per framework that dumps `ls -laR` and `exit 1`s on failure — so we never submit a framework Apple would reject, and a wrong guess is self-diagnosing instead of failing blind after a 6-minute notarization round-trip. Removed the obsolete copy-out loop and the old best-effort "seal proper framework bundles" loop.
- **Reason**: Rawhide nightly macOS build still failed notarization after the copy-out fix; the flat frameworks must be structurally repaired and sealed, not just have their binary re-signed.
- **Verification**: `python3 yaml.safe_load` parses; extracted shell `bash -n` clean. Autonomous build loop in progress (triggered + monitored) to confirm Apple accepts. Once green, port to release.yml + main's nightly.yml.
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

## 2026-06-24 (fix: macOS notarization rejected — PyInstaller flat-framework signatures were invalid)
- **Files changed**:
  - .github/workflows/nightly.yml — the macOS "Code Sign macOS App" step. Apple's notary log returned status=Invalid with five errors, all "The signature of the binary is invalid." on `*/Python.framework/Python` (dt_grpc, kokoro_tts, piper, sentiment_classifier, whisper_stt). Root cause: PyInstaller ships **flat** frameworks (the principal binary is a plain Mach-O, no Versions/ structure) carrying its own ad-hoc signature. `codesign` refuses to re-sign that binary in place ("bundle format is ambiguous"), so the broken signature survived — and Apple rejects a *bad* signature far more strictly than a missing one. The previous "best-effort tolerate after 4 retries" was therefore wrong: it left the invalid signature on the file. **Fix**: for any Mach-O inside a `*.framework/`, try signing in place (works for proper versioned frameworks + nested .so/.dylib); if codesign refuses, copy the binary OUT of the bundle, sign it as a standalone Mach-O (the Developer ID signature embeds in the file bytes), and copy it back. This is now a HARD requirement (`exit 1` if no valid signature can be produced) rather than a tolerated skip. Also: broadened the loose-Mach-O and catch-all passes to exclude `*.framework/*` (handled by the dedicated pass), and kept the timestamp-throttle retry/backoff on every codesign.
- **Reason**: Rawhide nightly macOS builds failed notarization with status=Invalid. The "main passed / Rawhide failed" discrepancy is explained by the cached ML-engine sidecars (`ML engines cache hit — skipping PyInstaller`): the last stable tag reused older cached sidecars with intact signatures, while the Rawhide run rebuilt them with a newer PyInstaller that emits flat frameworks with bad sigs.
- **Verification**: `python3 yaml.safe_load` parses; extracted shell `bash -n` clean. Awaiting a manual Rawhide build to confirm Apple accepts. Once green, port the same fix to release.yml (and main's nightly.yml).
- **Commit hash**: (uncommitted)

## 2026-06-23 (fix: needs-impact eval lowballed relief — going to the bathroom only refilled +8)
- **Files changed**:
  - lib/services/chat/llm_eval_engine.dart — added explicit RELIEF/RESTORATION magnitude guidance to BOTH needs-impact prompts (the main first-call prompt AND the Director-correction prompt, for parity). Needs run 0–100 (100 = satisfied); the prompt never said so and anchored low ("small effects stay small", "use small numbers or zeros"), so the model returned tiny deltas (e.g. bladder_delta +8) for a COMPLETE relief — leaving the character still "needing". Now the model is told a full relief must use a large delta: using the bathroom → bladder +60..+100; full meal → hunger +50..+90; sleeping / long rest → energy +60..+100 (broadly restores physical needs); thorough wash → hygiene +50..+90; deep connection/play → social/fun/comfort +20..+50. Small numbers (±1..±8) reserved for incidental effects. (1x baselines; still scaled by the user's strength factor; the +100 clamp already allowed this.)
- **Reason**: user report — going to the bathroom gave only +8 bladder (still needs to go), and sleeping (an OOC time-skip, which the user keeps passage-of-time OFF for on purpose) didn't refill needs. Both are the SAME root cause: the needs-impact eval, which reacts to the narrated scene, lowballed restorative activities. With passage-of-time off (intentional), a narrated sleep's energy refill must come from this eval — so the magnitude fix covers both. The annoying "manual reprocess every turn" was a workaround for this same lowballing.
- **Verification**: flutter analyze clean. Prompt-only change; needs clamp (-30..+100) and apply path unchanged. Parity kept across both needs prompts.
- **Not touched** (per user): passage-of-time is intentionally disabled — the OOC time-skip "ignored" log is expected, not a bug.

## 2026-06-23 (fix: loading a 1:1 chat nuked the character's saved realism state)
- **Files changed**:
  - lib/services/chat/chat_service_realism_dance.dart — In `_evaluateRealismForUpcomingSpeaker`, gated the `_groupRealism` load/save plumbing on `_activeGroup != null`. Previously the 1:1 host (`_activeGroup == null`) fell into the `else` branch and called `_loadGroupRealismIntoScalars(charId)`, then `_saveScalarsIntoGroupRealism(charId)` at the end. The group map's setters route through `_setGroupRealismValue`, which early-returns when `_activeGroup == null` (group-only store), while its getters (`getGroupAffectionScore` etc.) read the map with a 0/default fallback and are NOT gated. So for a 1:1 host the load read an empty map → reset bond→0, trust→default, fixation/emotion→empty, needs→fresh 100s, overwriting the state `loadSession` had just restored. Now the host operates directly on its scalar fields (the canonical 1:1 store), which already hold the loaded + post-decay values; the shared eval mutates them in place and `_saveChat` persists them as before. Group path unchanged.
  - lib/services/chat_service.dart — In `sendMessage`, removed the misleading 1:1-host "mirror post-decay realism into the cast store" block (`_saveScalarsIntoGroupRealism(_getCharacterId())` + its debugPrint). That mirror was a guaranteed no-op (the setter early-returns in 1:1) and only existed to feed the now-removed host reload. Kept the unified eval invocation (`_evaluateRealismForUpcomingSpeaker(_activeCharacter!)`).
- **Reason**: Regression introduced by the realism unification (commit ccae8b1 "collapse 1:1 + group onto ONE eval path"). The unified eval routed the 1:1 host through the group-only `_groupRealism` storage dance, but only the *read* side of that store has a 1:1 fallback; the *write* side is gated off in 1:1. The asymmetry meant the first post-load turn (and the realism UI) saw an empty store and wiped persisted bond/trust/emotion/fixation/needs. ## 2026-06-21 (fix: AI-generated characters dropped the first message + used literal names — CharacterGenService robustness)
- **Files changed**: lib/services/character_gen_service.dart.
- **Why**: (1) Generated characters sometimes had NO first message. Root cause: thinking models can return a stream containing only a `<think>` block (or hit premature EOS during the think prefill); `_callLLM` treated that non-empty raw as success, then `_cleanGreeting` stripped it to empty with no retry. (2) Description/personality embedded the literal character name instead of {{char}}, which can confuse the chat model mid-conversation.
- **What**: `_callLLM` now (a) bans the EOS token while reasoning is enabled (forces thinking models past the think block — same safeguard as the eval/fact paths), and (b) treats think-only output (nothing left after stripping think blocks) as a failure so the retry loop recovers instead of silently dropping the field. Added `_applyCharMacro` — a post-generation pass that replaces whole-word occurrences of the character's name (and significant name parts) with the portable {{char}} macro across description/personality/scenario/firstMessage/mesExample/alternateGreetings (the prompts already ask for {{char}} but models don't reliably comply).
- **Verification**: flutter analyze clean; flutter build macos --debug succeeds. Live generation behaviour verified by the user.
- **Branch**: main.
